genZNote: DNase positive when most of its Enterobacterales relatives aren't, and occasionally red enough to look like it's bleeding on the agar.

habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Widespread in moist environments; can colonize sinks, respiratory equipment, and disinfectant solutions in hospitals

culture.colonyMorphology: Some strains produce a distinctive red pigment (prodigiosin), especially at room temperature; many clinical isolates are non-pigmented
culture.pigmentation: Red (prodigiosin) in pigmented strains; non-pigmented in many clinical isolates

identificationClues: DNase positive — one of the few Enterobacterales with this feature, useful in identification
Some strains produce a characteristic red pigment (prodigiosin) at room temperature
Late or weak lactose fermentation on MacConkey agar
Notable for colonizing hospital water sources and even some disinfectant/antiseptic solutions

diseases: Outbreaks associated with contaminated medical equipment/solutions
virulenceFactors: Various proteases and lipases contributing to tissue damage
clinicalImportance.transmission: Nosocomial — contaminated water sources, respiratory equipment, intravenous fluids, or even contaminated antiseptic solutions
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: A recognized cause of healthcare-associated outbreaks, notable historically for causing infections via contamination of items assumed to be sterile, such as multi-dose medication vials
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: DNase positivity plus (when present) the classic red pigment help distinguish it from other Enterobacterales on routine workup

examFacts.distinguishingFeature: DNase positivity distinguishes it from most other Enterobacterales; some strains produce a distinctive red pigment
